sentence: This project studies how coral fragments attach, heal and grow, and how the chemical environment around them affects their skeleton.
This project studies how academic coaching affects retention, academic standing, and graduation in engineering.
This project studies and engineers proteins that emit light when they bind calcium ions in marine organisms called siphonophores.
This project studies semiconductor-based sensors, microelectronic circuits, and how AI can analyze sensor data.
This project studies how lithium moves through multilayer systems with nano-sized layers, using neutron reflectometry and numerical modeling.
This project builds a method that uses chemical reactions and mass spectrometry imaging to map molecules that differ only in structure within tissues.
This project builds a security data lake of cyberattacks on supercomputing systems so research teams can test AI-based detection models.
This project builds a model to test how groundwater beneath the Antarctic Ice Sheet changes the flow of ice.
This project looks for two-dimensional ferroelectric materials and studies how their polarization affects electrical conductivity.
This project builds AI weather models that follow atmospheric physics to find out when the stratosphere helps predict surface weather.
This project studies how the protein septin senses the curvature of a cell membrane as it assembles into filaments.
This project studies how first year seminars, major success maps, and service-learning affect retention and graduation rates.
This project builds machine learning models that predict properties of organic compounds and help explain how air pollution forms.
This project builds methods that make AI systems that read medical images clearer to understand and easier to correct.
This project studies how insurance can help organizations manage cyber risks to critical infrastructure.
This project studies how surfaces reflect polarized light and how that can help computers recognize objects and understand scenes.
This project studies how proteins that lie in only a few orientations affect cryogenic electron microscopy maps, and builds ways to correct this.
This project uses microrobotics and machine learning to study how cells form patterns and to build a liver organoid.
